_comment: Which modpack models go into the planner's 3D library. Edit this instead of rebuilding the tool.
'exclude' entries are matched as substrings against the model's logical path, lower case,
with backslashes and a leading backslash (so '\weapons\' also matches a top-level weapons folder).
minExtent drops anything whose largest visual bounding-box side is under that many metres.
Now 0.05 (was 1.0, then 0.4) so every prop a mission can place gets a real shape:
barrels, chairs, sacks, ammo crates and bagfence end caps sit between 0.4 m and 1 m, and the
0.05 cut keeps only genuinely degenerate models out. Gear is kept out by the path excludes
below, not by size. The bounding box is now measured on the geometry that is actually kept,
with proxy placeholders dropped, so the cut compares against the shape players see.
meshBudget is the triangle count above which a mesh is vertex-clustered down. At 20000 it was
decimating 948 models - every vehicle and tank, the exact models whose detailed view looked
wrong - so it is now 400000, which leaves effectively everything at full visual-LOD detail
and only guards against a pathological model. Library size is not a constraint: a rebuild is
a one-off that gets pushed to the planner once, and the per-plan download is the voxel bundle,
not the meshes, which are fetched one model at a time only in detailed mode.
Weapon optics are excluded by path rather than by size because a handful of them hard-crash
the p3d reader (Windows fast-fail). They are irrelevant to a map view, so dropping them
early is cheaper than letting the resume journal quarantine them one restart at a time.
